rows.text: makes the call at `001D6B70` + 0x4 (no arguments set up) and returns 1 when byte `+0x88` of the pointer it returns is non-zero, else 0
makes the call at `001D6D20` + 0x1F (no arguments set up) and returns `0020C1B0(that result, rcx, edx, r8, r9)`, the incoming `r9` going to the callee as its fifth (stack) argument

for each of four names at a 6-byte stride from `01DFCFE8` ("c1004"), calls `001DB050` + 0x4D (256-byte stack buffer, 0, 0x100), copies "PS2Data\obj_finish\in\chara\c10\" (`01DFD010`) into the buffer and appends the name and the word 0x005C (`008FB2B0`); only when the string at `rdx` is longer (unsigned) than the built string, calls `001DB050` + 0xFE the same way on a second 256-byte buffer, makes the call at `001DB050` + 0x111 (through qword `008C2F70`) with (second buffer, `rdx`, the built string's length) and byte-compares the two buffers to the terminating zero, returning 1 when they are equal; returns 0 when no name matches (`rcx` is not read)

walks a binary tree from qword `rcx+0x20` until it reaches the sentinel `rcx+8`, comparing the 128-bit key at `rdx` (qword `+0`, then qword `+8`) signed against each node's qwords `+0x18` then `+0x20` and descending to the node's qword `+8` when the node is less than the key and to its qword `+0` when greater; on an exact match it tail-jumps at `001F47D0` + 0x64 with `rcx` unchanged and `rdx` set to the node's qword `+0x28`; returns 0 when the sentinel is reached
